name: Phonk
summary: Two lanes under one name: driving 2020s drift phonk (130-155 BPM, distorted/clipped 808 kick, half-time or four-on-floor drums, TR-808 cowbell riff as the lead melodic hook) and slow, murky classic Memphis phonk (60-80 BPM half-time, SpaceGhostPurrp/DJ Screw/DJ Spanish Fly lineage, heavy swing, tape-hiss ghost notes). The 808 cowbell riff is the genre's hook in both lanes — carried here on the cowbell role.

sounds.kick: Drift phonk: distorted, clipped, near-max velocity 808 kick, four-on-floor or half-time. Memphis: soft, slow, half-time boom-bap kick spaced far apart.
sounds.snare: Drift phonk: hits beat 3 in half-time voicings, or 2-and-4 in four-on-floor voicings. Memphis: a single lazy hit per bar, often dragging behind the grid under heavy swing.
sounds.hats: Drift phonk: 8th-to-16th hat rolls, trap-derived. Memphis: sparse, unevenly-velocity-ghosted 16ths for a lo-fi, tape-degraded feel.
sounds.percussion: The TR-808 cowbell riff is the lead melodic percussion in both lanes — this engine represents its rhythm on the cowbell role; pitch content comes from a chromatically-mapped sampler.
sounds.cymbals: Essentially unused in either lane; open hat appears only rarely as a build-up accent.

machines: Roland TR-808 — the cowbell riff, kick and snare source across both lanes
E-mu SP-1200 / Akai MPC60 — chopping 90s Memphis rap tapes and jazz/funk samples
E-mu Drumulator / Akai S900 — period-correct lo-fi drum sampling for the Memphis lane
Sonic Academy Kick 2 / distortion plugins — modern distorted 808 kick design for drift phonk
Phonk cowbell one-shot packs (Memphis + Brazilian-phonk crossover) — the genre's actual melodic hook material
references: DJ Spanish Fly — late-1980s Memphis 808/cowbell foundations
DJ Screw — chopped and screwed Houston lineage
SpaceGhostPurrp — Mysterious Phonk: Chronicles of SpaceGhostPurrp (2012)
